- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.67) but price declines, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to offset sentiment-driven overconfidence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast often lags true price; adjust by adding 1–2% to forecast to catch early trend reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates downward trends after sentiment turns bearish; apply 2–4% upward bias to counteract lagged bearish sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or negative values, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 3–5% to compensate for pessimism bias.
